# EVOLVED_COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_TIMELINE

| DATE | EVENT | LINEAGE_CLASS | EVOLVED_DISPOSITION | SOURCES |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1910s-1930s | Industrial psychology, physiology, anthropometry, time-and-motion and early aviation medicine develop partially separate traditions; no single CSE lineage yet. | CLASSICAL_HUMAN_FACTORS_LINEAGE | Historical background; later syntheses should not retroactively label all work CSE. | S001 |
| 1939-1945 | Wartime aviation, radar, gunnery, controls, selection and training expose failures caused by mismatch among people, machines, information and environments. | CLASSICAL_HUMAN_FACTORS_LINEAGE | Establishes human performance and equipment design as coupled military/engineering problems, not merely UI aesthetics. | S001 |
| 1951 | Fitts edits *Human Engineering for an Effective Air-navigation and Traffic-control System*, including influential comparative human/machine functions. | CLASSICAL_HUMAN_FACTORS_LINEAGE | Historically important function-allocation heuristic; later rejected as a universal rule. | S002 |
| 1957 | The Human Factors Society is founded in the United States, institutionalising a field spanning displays, controls, performance, selection, training and system design. | CLASSICAL_HUMAN_FACTORS_LINEAGE | Professional consolidation; not a singular intellectual origin. | S001 |
| 1960s-1970s | Supervisory-control research studies humans setting goals and monitoring computers that execute lower-level control. | SUPERVISORY_CONTROL_LINEAGE | Moves beyond manual control but creates monitoring, feedback and authority problems. | S003 |
| 1978 | Sheridan and Verplank publish a graded human/computer control taxonomy for teleoperators. | SUPERVISORY_CONTROL_LINEAGE | Important descriptive precursor to levels-of-automation research; insufficient as coordination design. | S003 |
| 1983 | Rasmussen publishes the skill/rule/knowledge framework and distinctions among signals, signs and symbols. | COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE | Connects representations to modes of performance and adaptation. | S004 |
| 1983 | Hollnagel and Woods publish “Cognitive Systems Engineering: New Wine in New Bottles.” | COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE | Programme statement for analysing cognitive systems and interaction rather than isolated components. | S005 |
| 1983 | Bainbridge publishes “Ironies of Automation.” | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_LINEAGE | Shows that automation can leave humans with monitoring and rare difficult recovery while eroding practice. | S008 |
| 1988 | Woods and Roth frame cognitive engineering around human problem solving with tools in complex worlds. | COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE | Strengthens field-study and design focus on cognitive work demands. | S007 |
| 1988-1995 | Endsley develops a three-level individual situation-awareness model and SAGAT-oriented measurement programme. | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_LINEAGE | Highly influential construct; retained only with explicit construct/measurement caveats. | S029 S030 S031 |
| 1991 | Clark and Brennan systematise grounding and medium-dependent costs in communication. | TEAM_COGNITION_OR_COMMON_GROUND_LINEAGE | Contributes transferable mechanisms for acknowledgement, referents and repair. | S037 |
| 1992 | Vicente and Rasmussen formalise ecological interface design from work-domain constraints and means-ends relations. | ECOLOGICAL_INTERFACE_LINEAGE | Supports novel-state diagnosis; implementation evidence remains domain-bound. | S018 |
| 1994 | Rasmussen, Pejtersen and Goodstein consolidate CSE/CWA methods, including abstraction and decomposition hierarchies. | COGNITIVE_WORK_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE | Major documentary source for constraint-centred work analysis. | S006 |
| 1995 | Hutchins publishes *Cognition in the Wild* and cockpit studies of distributed representations. | DISTRIBUTED_COGNITION_LINEAGE | Distinct ethnographic lineage locating cognitive function across people and artefacts. | S025 S026 |
| 1995 | Sarter and Woods analyse mode error; Endsley and Kiris experimentally examine out-of-the-loop performance. | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_LINEAGE | Makes mode legibility, monitoring and takeover readiness central empirical problems. | S009 S010 |
| 1996-1997 | Billings articulates human-centred aviation automation; Sarter, Woods and Billings synthesise automation surprise. | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_LINEAGE | Emphasises predictability, feedback, authority and crew-centred coordination. | S011 S079 S088 |
| 1997-2000 | Parasuraman and Riley distinguish use, misuse, disuse and abuse; Parasuraman, Sheridan and Wickens formalise types/stages/levels of automation. | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_LINEAGE | Useful taxonomy and reliance vocabulary, later subordinated to coordination and context. | S013 S014 |
| 2002 | Dekker and Woods criticise MABA-MABA allocation; Dekker advances local-rationality/new-view accident analysis. | COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE | Shifts allocation toward coordination and human-error analysis toward mechanism/context. | S015 S070 |
| 2004 | Klein and colleagues state ten challenges for automation as a team player. | TEAM_COGNITION_OR_COMMON_GROUND_LINEAGE | Introduces interdependence, predictability, common ground and directability requirements. | S038 |
| 2005-2006 | Hollnagel and Woods publish the joint-cognitive-systems foundations/patterns books. | COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE | Explicitly develops the joint system as unit of analysis and design. | S027 S028 |
| 2008-2017 | EID/CWA applications and reviews expand across nuclear/process and other domains while exposing scalability, analyst-dependence and maintenance limits. | COGNITIVE_WORK_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE | Supports property-level retention rather than mandatory full-method adoption. | S019 S020 S021 S022 S023 S024 |
| 2009-2014 | Healthcare handoff/checklist programmes produce both strong positive and null/heterogeneous results. | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC | Shows that explicit coordination can pay off, but named bundles and completion metrics are not universal properties. | S065 S068 S069 |
| 2010-2015 | Trust, complacency, automation bias, algorithm aversion and forcing-function studies refine “trust” into calibrated reliance and verification. | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_LINEAGE | Rejects trust maximisation and generic transparency as objectives. | S039 S040 S041 S042 S043 S045 S085 |
| 2012-2017 | Alarm-fatigue reviews, process-industry standards and FAA alerting guidance consolidate action-, priority- and lifecycle-oriented alarm management. | CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING | Cross-domain convergence on attention as a scarce controlled resource. | S060 S061 S062 S087 |
| 2014-2024 | Adaptive automation and human-autonomy teaming research moves toward mixed initiative, interdependence and coactive design, but remains heterogeneous. | HUMAN_AUTONOMY_TRANSLATION | Dynamic authority is retained only with bounded triggers and legible transitions. | S051 S052 S053 |
| 2018 | Woods develops graceful extensibility, sharpening adaptive-capacity and boundary-awareness questions. | RESILIENCE_OR_ADAPTIVE_LINEAGE | Hybrid contribution: visible margins and extensible capacity, not generic resilience branding. | S073 |
| 2020 | The NTSB Atlas Air 3591 report documents an unexpected go-around mode change that was annunciated but not effectively recognised, with only seconds to recover. | ACCIDENT_OR_INCIDENT_EVIDENCE | Strong evidence that visible mode names do not by themselves establish mode understanding. | S076 |
| 2021-2024 | Human-AI explanation experiments show mixed effects; cognitive forcing and selected explanations can reduce overreliance, but explanation is not uniformly beneficial. | HUMAN_AUTONOMY_TRANSLATION | Supports decision-linked explanation and verifiability rather than “show reasoning.” | S044 S045 S046 S047 |
| 2024 | A systematic review/meta-analysis finds human-AI combinations underperform the better solo component on average, with substantial task heterogeneity. | HUMAN_AUTONOMY_TRANSLATION | Directly rejects automatic synergy and makes joint-system evaluation a prerequisite. | S048 |
| 2026 | A cross-domain meta-review of situation-awareness measurement reports heterogeneous evidence and reinforces the need for explicit psychometric and use-case limits. | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_LINEAGE | Measurement dispute remains open; narrower state-access and prediction properties survive. | S036 |

The timeline distinguishes direct transmission, adjacent lineages and later domain translation. Conceptual similarity alone was not treated as documentary ancestry.

# EVOLVED_COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_GENEALOGY

| LINEAGE_CLASS | DATED_SPAN | CORE_PROBLEM | DOCUMENTARY_TRANSMISSION | DISTINCT_CONTRIBUTION | RELATION_TO_EVOLVED_FORM | SOURCES |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CLASSICAL_HUMAN_FACTORS_LINEAGE | 1930s-present | Fit among human performance, displays, controls, workspaces, selection, training and system demands. | Professional histories and primary wartime/post-war engineering reports establish continuity into modern HF/E. | Perception, anthropometry, workload, control-display compatibility, error tolerance and evaluation. | Ancestry, but evolved CSE is not reducible to usability or isolated operator optimisation. | S001 S002 S074 S075 |
| SUPERVISORY_CONTROL_LINEAGE | 1960s-present | Human goal setting, monitoring and intervention when computers execute lower-level control. | Sheridan/Verplank and later automation taxonomies directly transmit supervisory-control concepts. | Graded control, monitoring, intervention and automation-policy vocabulary. | Retained as descriptive input; superseded as a complete prescription by coordination and authority-transition design. | S003 S014 S049 S050 |
| COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE | 1983-present | How people and machines jointly perform cognitive work in complex dynamic environments. | Hollnagel/Woods programme articles and books, Rasmussen/Pejtersen/Goodstein, Woods/Roth and domain translations. | Work demands, cognitive coupling, field studies, joint cognitive systems and mechanism-centred design. | Primary native lineage. | S005 S006 S007 S027 S028 S080 |
| COGNITIVE_WORK_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE | 1980s-present | Represent constraints, control tasks, strategies, social organisation and competencies without prescribing one sequence. | Rasmussen et al. through Naikar and applied CWA literature. | Abstraction/decomposition and constraint-centred work-domain modelling. | Underlying modelling property retained; full canonical method context-dependent and bureaucracy-prone. | S006 S019 S020 S024 |
| ECOLOGICAL_INTERFACE_LINEAGE | 1992-present | Make work-domain constraints and means-ends relations perceptually available for routine and novel problem solving. | Vicente/Rasmussen theory, later Bennett/Flach synthesis and domain evaluations. | Constraint/affordance representation and support for knowledge-based adaptation. | Constraint representation retained; canonical EID display family remains context-dependent. | S018 S021 S022 S023 |
| DISTRIBUTED_COGNITION_LINEAGE | 1980s-1990s-present | How cognitive function is distributed across people, representations and time in real work. | Hutchins ethnography and cockpit/navigation analyses; conceptual convergence with JCS is documented but not identity. | External memory, representational transformation and distributed unit of analysis. | Directly informs distributed-state and shared-artefact properties; remains a distinct analytical tradition. | S025 S026 |
| TEAM_COGNITION_OR_COMMON_GROUND_LINEAGE | 1991-present | How interdependent participants establish referents, commitments, shared constraints and repair misunderstanding. | Clark/Brennan grounding, joint-activity/team-player research, CRM/handoff applications. | Grounding, mutual predictability/directability, challenge, readback and handoff semantics. | Imported and hybridised where coordination requires more than information availability. | S037 S038 S052 S065 S066 S067 |
| HUMAN_AUTOMATION_LINEAGE | 1980s-present | Mode error, monitoring, out-of-loop performance, reliance, adaptive automation and takeover. | Bainbridge, Sarter/Woods, Endsley/Kiris, Billings, Parasuraman and later empirical reviews. | Residual work, mode/intent legibility, calibrated reliance and takeover readiness. | Primary evidence source for state, authority and human-capability properties. | S008 S009 S010 S011 S013 S039 S041 |
| HUMAN_AUTONOMY_TRANSLATION | 2010s-present | Interdependence with adaptive/autonomous/AI systems whose policies, capabilities and explanations vary. | Coactive design and human-autonomy teaming explicitly extend joint-activity concepts; XAI is only partly lineage-linked. | Mutual observability/predictability/directability, bounded mixed initiative and evaluation against solo baselines. | Domain translation, not proof that contemporary AI constructs descend directly from CSE. | S044 S045 S048 S051 S052 S053 |
| RESILIENCE_OR_ADAPTIVE_LINEAGE | 2000s-present | Adaptation, capacity margins, work-as-done and recovery under disturbances beyond nominal procedures. | Hollnagel, Woods and allied field literature share authors and concepts with CSE but form a hybrid rather than one genealogy. | Boundary awareness, local adaptation, graceful degradation and learning from normal work. | Hybrid contribution retained where it yields explicit capacity, authority or recovery properties. | S072 S073 |
| CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING | Cross-period | Feedback closure, provenance, alert lifecycle, configuration/freshness and verification arise in control, operations and safety practice as well as CSE. | Often conceptual convergence or shared systems ancestry rather than direct CSE transmission. | Operational state semantics and lifecycle governance that make cognitive properties executable. | Admitted as convergent properties with lineage labels preserved; no false genealogy claimed. | S012 S061 S062 S071 S074 S075 S081 S087 |
| DOMAIN_SPECIFIC | Variable | Aviation CRM, healthcare handoffs, nuclear EID and automated-driving takeover operationalise selected mechanisms. | Direct within their domains; cross-domain copying requires new evidence. | Field tests, accident evidence and implementation boundary conditions. | Mechanisms may transfer; named bundles, thresholds and rituals do not automatically transfer. | S022 S023 S054 S055 S065 S066 S067 S068 S069 S076 S077 S078 S084 |

No single genealogy was forced. CSE/JCS, CWA, EID, distributed cognition, team/common-ground work, human-automation research and resilience are overlapping but materially distinct. XAI and human-agent supervision are modern translations unless direct lineage is documented.

# INDIVIDUAL_HUMAN_FACTORS_VS_JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS

| DIMENSION | ISOLATED_HUMAN_OR_INTERFACE_FRAME | JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_FRAME | FROZEN_EVOLVED_JUDGEMENT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unit of analysis | One operator, screen, task or cognitive construct. | People, automation/agents, procedures, representations, organisation and environment coupled around a work function. | Joint frame is primary when consequential dependencies cross components; isolated analysis remains valid for bounded perceptual/ergonomic questions. |
| Performance | Human error rate, response time, workload or satisfaction. | Joint decision/action outcome, coordination cost, transition quality, recovery and system-level error. | Component measures diagnose mechanisms but cannot establish joint-system value alone. |
| State | What the user perceives or remembers. | Where state is represented, who can access it, freshness/provenance, transformations and who needs it by when. | Distributed state is an engineering object; information existing somewhere is not sufficient. |
| Automation | Tool performing an allocated task. | Interdependent participant whose policy changes human work, authority and residual tasks. | Automation capability does not imply pairing benefit or appropriate authority. |
| Function allocation | Choose human or machine by comparative strengths. | Design who senses, decides, acts, verifies, coordinates and recovers across states and transitions. | Static allocation is superseded as a complete method. |
| Mental model / SA | Property located in the individual. | Prediction and access obligations may be distributed across people and artefacts; global construct remains contested. | Retain testable prediction/state-access requirements, not post-hoc “lost SA” labels. |
| Authority | Document who is responsible or has final say. | Align real-time state access, competence, controls, time, stop/escalation rights and accountability. | Nominal authority without capability is invalid. |
| Handoff | Send information or complete a form. | Transfer state, evidence status, authority, pending obligations and unresolved anomalies with acceptance and repair. | Receipt is not acceptance; acceptance is not independent verification. |
| Adaptation | Deviation from prescribed correct work. | Local response to variable demands within constraints, margins and authority. | Neither compliance nor adaptation is automatically safe; both need outcome and boundary evidence. |
| Evaluation | Usability/construct score after use. | Compare joint system with relevant human-alone/automation-alone baselines and measure consequential decisions. | Outcome-first evaluation is strongly retained. |
| Responsibility | Attribute error to the last human action. | Reconstruct local rationality and distributed conditions while preserving specific accountability. | Human error is not terminal causal closure. |
| Cheap path | Often absent; apply the standard method. | Scale joint analysis to consequence, coupling and observability. | A direct deterministic state/effect contract may be enough for trivial work. |

# EVOLVED_COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_PROPERTY_LEDGER

## Frozen denominator summary

| PROPERTY_ID | PROPERTY_NAME | CURRENT_STATUS | TRIGGER | CHEAP_PATH | MATURE_FORM | KEY_SOURCES |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ECSE-01 | Joint cognitive work system as the unit of design | JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROPERTY | Consequential work in which decisions, representations, authority or control are distributed across two or more participants or artefacts. | For a low-consequence, single-actor, transparent deterministic operation, document the actor, state and effect without constructing a full joint-system model. | Define the work system boundary, cognitive functions, authority, information flows, dependencies, timing and adaptation; test joint performance, not merely component usability. | [S005], [S006], [S007], [S025], [S026], [S027] |
| ECSE-02 | Decision-relevant work-domain and constraint modelling | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | Complex, variable or safety/consequence-sensitive work in which unanticipated states or multiple strategies are plausible. | For stable routine work, a concise state-transition model, invariant list or decision table may preserve the property without a full CWA programme. | Maintain an auditable, decision-consumed constraint model at the smallest useful granularity; link representations and procedures to it. | [S004], [S006], [S018], [S019], [S020], [S021] |
| ECSE-03 | Distributed representations and external cognitive support | STRONGLY_RETAINED | Work with multi-step obligations, interruptions, team coordination, long time spans or high memory demand. | Do not externalise trivial facts when the representation costs more attention than it saves; use a small status marker or no artefact. | Design external memory around live tasks, ownership, update semantics, freshness and recovery; test whether it reduces errors rather than merely adding documentation. | [S007], [S025], [S026], [S027], [S037], [S063] |
| ECSE-04 | Coordination design beyond function allocation | JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROPERTY | Any consequential split of work between humans, automation, teams or agents. | A fully encapsulated, deterministic service with verified input/output contracts may need only interface and failure semantics rather than rich teaming protocol. | Use function allocation as an input, then close the coordination contracts, transitions, feedback and recovery for the joint activity. | [S002], [S003], [S014], [S015], [S016], [S038] |
| ECSE-05 | Dynamic role, function and authority coordination | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_CONTEXT_PROPERTY | Variable environments where relative human/automation capability changes materially and the cost of fixed allocation is high. | Keep roles fixed when they are adequate, when transition risk exceeds benefit, or when authority changes cannot be made legible in time. | Use bounded, state-dependent mixed initiative with explicit transition contracts and post-change confirmation—not opaque adaptive reassignment. | [S003], [S014], [S049], [S050], [S051], [S052] |
| ECSE-06 | Residual-task and workload-migration analysis | STRONGLY_RETAINED | Any automation proposal that claims workload reduction, staffing reduction or safer human oversight. | For a transparent deterministic substitution with no material residual task, record the proof and avoid a heavyweight study. | Accept automation only with an explicit residual-work account, peak-load evaluation and named owner for newly created cognitive work. | [S008], [S010], [S013], [S014], [S015], [S017] |
| ECSE-07 | Decision-relevant state, mode, intent and consequence legibility | STATE_MODE_LEGIBILITY_PROPERTY | Whenever automation state changes the meaning, effect or permissibility of a consequential action. | For a stateless or single-mode operation, show the immediate action/effect and omit a mode apparatus. | Provide consequence-oriented mode legibility at the decision point, validated under realistic attention, stress and transition conditions. | [S009], [S011], [S012], [S076], [S077], [S078] |
| ECSE-08 | Transition, pending-action and commitment visibility | STATE_MODE_LEGIBILITY_PROPERTY | Asynchronous, delayed, queued, autonomous or multi-stage consequential actions. | For atomic local actions with immediate direct physical feedback, the effect itself may be sufficient. | Close each consequential transition with status, timing, owner and world-effect evidence proportional to risk. | [S009], [S012], [S038], [S052], [S076], [S079] |
| ECSE-09 | Freshness, provenance, uncertainty and degradation visibility | STATE_MODE_LEGIBILITY_PROPERTY | When decisions depend on remote, cached, fused, model-generated, asynchronous or potentially degraded information. | For direct, current, self-evident local state, omit provenance decoration unless a failure mode makes it material. | Surface only uncertainty and lineage that changes action or verification; provide drill-down for disputes and degraded operation. | [S011], [S012], [S039], [S040], [S044], [S046] |
| ECSE-10 | Command-to-world feedback closure | STATE_MODE_LEGIBILITY_PROPERTY | Remote, automated, safety-critical, delayed or externally coupled actions where acceptance is not equivalent to success. | For direct reversible manipulation with immediate reliable perceptual feedback, the world effect can close the loop without additional reporting. | Define completion in terms of the intended state and provide independent effect evidence proportional to consequence. | [S001], [S003], [S007], [S012], [S038], [S052] |
| ECSE-11 | Authority, responsibility, observability and capability alignment | AUTHORITY_HANDOFF_PROPERTY | Consequential automation, delegated decisions, multi-party control and exception recovery. | For reversible low-consequence suggestions, ordinary user choice and clear undo may be sufficient. | Use state-dependent authority contracts that specify who decides, who acts, who verifies, who may stop, and what capability evidence is required. | [S011], [S012], [S038], [S039], [S052], [S053] |
| ECSE-12 | Genuine human intervention capability rather than ceremonial oversight | AUTHORITY_HANDOFF_PROPERTY | Only when human intervention is claimed as a control for consequential automation. | Remove the approval step when risk is low or intervention cannot be made real; use engineered automatic constraints or independent safeguards instead. | Treat human oversight as a tested control relationship with explicit preconditions and failure criteria, not a ritual placement. | [S008], [S010], [S011], [S012], [S038], [S045] |
| ECSE-13 | Explicit and verified handoff of state, authority and obligations | AUTHORITY_HANDOFF_PROPERTY | Cross-person, cross-agent, cross-session or cross-shift transfer of consequential work or control. | For trivial same-context continuation with visible shared state, a brief acknowledgement or no formal handoff may suffice. | Use a proportional handoff contract with explicit ownership, acceptance, verification and discrepancy repair; distinguish transmitted claims from checked state. | [S037], [S038], [S052], [S065], [S067], [S068] |
| ECSE-14 | Takeover and re-entry readiness with state reacquisition and time budget | AUTHORITY_HANDOFF_PROPERTY | Whenever a human is the fallback for rare automation limits or failures. | Do not claim human fallback when the time budget or readiness cannot be sustained; use fail-safe automation, controlled degradation or another continuously engaged controller. | Design graded handback with early warning, compact state reconstruction, safe transition envelope, practice and demonstrated recovery performance. | [S008], [S010], [S049], [S050], [S054], [S055] |
| ECSE-15 | Skill, knowledge and readiness maintenance for retained human functions | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_CONTEXT_PROPERTY | When humans retain consequential monitoring, diagnosis, takeover or recovery duties that occur too rarely for natural practice. | No special rehearsal is needed when the human is not a fallback, the task is self-evident/reversible, or competence is continuously exercised. | Use targeted, scenario-based readiness maintenance tied to actual fallback roles and changing automation, with periodic demonstrated performance. | [S008], [S010], [S054], [S055], [S066], [S067] |
| ECSE-16 | Calibrated reliance and verifiability rather than maximal trust | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_CONTEXT_PROPERTY | When automation advice or action is fallible and users can choose to rely, verify, override or abstain. | For deterministic, independently enforced functions, avoid trust messaging and expose simple guarantees/failure semantics. | Optimise appropriate reliance and decision quality, not subjective trust level; make verification cheaper where consequences are high. | [S013], [S039], [S040], [S041], [S042], [S043] |
| ECSE-17 | Countermeasures to automation bias, disuse and correlated judgement | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | Consequential judgement where automation error is plausible and independent evidence or alternative hypotheses can discriminate. | Do not impose independence when shared known risks or authoritative facts are necessary, or when low consequence makes forcing costs exceed value. | Preserve shared factual constraints while protecting conclusion-neutral evidence generation when diversity has value; synthesise after independent returns. | [S041], [S042], [S043], [S045], [S047], [S083] |
| ECSE-18 | Actionable, prioritised, routed and escalated alerting | STRONGLY_RETAINED | Conditions requiring attention or intervention that would not otherwise be reliably perceived in time. | Use passive status, batching, audit logs or no notification when no immediate decision consumer or action exists. | Engineer alert portfolios as attention-allocation systems with lifecycle ownership, scenario/flood tests and outcome-linked escalation. | [S059], [S060], [S061], [S062], [S087], [S086] |
| ECSE-19 | Alarm lifecycle rationalisation, monitoring and retirement | STRONGLY_RETAINED | Any persistent alerting environment with changing systems, thresholds, staffing or operational context. | For a small static system with a handful of self-evident alerts, periodic simple review is sufficient. | Treat alerts as maintained operational controls whose continued existence must be justified by a live decision and response path. | [S060], [S061], [S062], [S086], [S087] |
| ECSE-20 | Interruption timing and resumption support | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | Multi-step consequential work exposed to alerts, messages, handoffs or task switching. | Do not add resumption machinery to brief reversible tasks; batch low-urgency notifications or allow natural task boundaries. | Design interruptibility and recovery as part of workflow and alert policy, with minimal state cues at the locus of resumption. | [S063], [S064], [S086], [S087] |
| ECSE-21 | Peak workload, transition load and reserve-capacity engineering | STRONGLY_RETAINED | Time-critical, multi-task or interruption-prone work where overload can delay or distort consequential action. | For low-pace work with ample slack, use direct task performance and simple staffing evidence rather than elaborate workload instrumentation. | Engineer peak demand and reserve capacity using converging performance, behavioural and subjective evidence, not a single average score. | [S008], [S017], [S050], [S056], [S057], [S058] |
| ECSE-22 | Underload, vigilance and engagement management | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_CONTEXT_PROPERTY | Long-duration monitoring with rare signals and consequential need for detection or takeover. | Do not create artificial activity when no human monitoring control is needed; remove ceremonial monitoring instead. | Either design sustained, meaningful engagement with measurable readiness or eliminate the human-monitor fallback claim. | [S008], [S010], [S017], [S050], [S058], [S059] |
| ECSE-23 | Grounded common ground with discrepancy detection and repair | JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROPERTY | Interdependent work in which one participant's action depends on another's interpretation, commitment or state claim. | For co-located, low-risk, directly visible action, natural feedback can ground understanding without formal protocol. | Build recoverable common ground around authoritative facts and commitments while preserving explicit uncertainty and dissent. | [S025], [S026], [S037], [S038], [S052], [S053] |
| ECSE-24 | Shared factual state separated from interpretations and favoured hypotheses | JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROPERTY | Multi-reviewer, multi-agent or team analysis where independent discrimination and later synthesis both matter. | For execution of an already decided plan, broad hypothesis independence may add no value; share the approved intent and constraints directly. | Use a common factual/authority substrate plus explicitly separated interpretation channels and a traceable synthesis step. | [S025], [S037], [S038], [S052], [S083], [S086] |
| ECSE-25 | Independent exploratory judgement where evidence diversity has value | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | High-uncertainty judgement with plausible alternatives, material anchoring risk and enough time for independent evidence acquisition. | Do not isolate reviewers from relevant known hazards, authoritative constraints or evidence necessary to avoid repeating known mistakes; skip independence for routine deterministic checks. | Use staged independence: shared facts/constraints, independent exploration, explicit overlap analysis, adversarial review of returned candidates, and accountable synthesis. | [S042], [S045], [S083], [S085] |
| ECSE-26 | Constraint- and affordance-oriented representation for adaptive diagnosis | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | Complex dynamic systems with coupled constraints and credible off-nominal conditions not exhaustively scriptable. | For simple discrete workflows, a state diagram, decision table or direct manipulation may capture the constraints more cheaply than an ecological display. | Use the smallest validated representation that makes action-relevant system relationships and boundaries perceivable under disturbance. | [S004], [S018], [S021], [S022], [S023], [S080] |
| ECSE-27 | Procedural baselines combined with governed adaptation | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | Variable consequential work where procedures are necessary but anomalies or trade-offs cannot be fully scripted. | For stable deterministic tasks, a concise executable procedure with direct verification may be enough; for expert exploratory work, use constraints rather than over-prescription. | Treat procedures as tested resources within a constraint-governed adaptive system, not as exhaustive descriptions of safe work. | [S004], [S006], [S070], [S071], [S072], [S073] |
| ECSE-28 | Decision-linked explanation, intent, limits and provenance | HUMAN_AUTOMATION_CONTEXT_PROPERTY | Consequential recommendations or autonomous actions whose basis, limits or future behaviour affect reliance, challenge or coordination. | For deterministic functions with inspectable contracts, show inputs, rule, result and failure state; omit narrative explanation. | Use task-timed, contestable and outcome-tested legibility rather than generic explanation volume or chain-of-thought display. | [S038], [S039], [S044], [S045], [S046], [S047] |
| ECSE-29 | Reliability-change signalling, recalibration and trust repair | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | Systems whose performance varies by state, population, version, environment or recent degradation. | For stable deterministic components with formal guarantees, version/failure notices may suffice without trust-repair programmes. | Make reliance policies version- and state-sensitive, with explicit change points, temporary safeguards and evidence-based restoration. | [S013], [S039], [S040], [S043], [S047], [S085] |
| ECSE-30 | Mutual observability, predictability and directability in joint activity | JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROPERTY | Joint human-agent or multi-agent work with interdependent plans and changing local information. | For a stable encapsulated tool, an input/output contract and cancel/error path may provide enough observability and directability. | Design these as reciprocal, role-specific coordination affordances, not unilateral surveillance or unrestricted control. | [S038], [S052], [S053], [S081] |
| ECSE-31 | Operational process-model alignment and repair | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | When safe action depends on predicting automation or process response beyond immediate direct feedback. | For simple self-revealing systems, direct state/effect feedback may remove the need to assess an internal model. | Treat model alignment as testable prediction competence supported by current representations and feedback, not as presumed understanding. | [S004], [S007], [S009], [S010], [S011], [S079] |
| ECSE-32 | Learning from coordination failures, near misses and automation surprises | STRONGLY_RETAINED | Incidents, near misses, unexpected automation behaviour, workarounds or recurrent handoff/alert failures. | For trivial reversible errors, a local correction and lightweight pattern check may be enough. | Use mechanism-centred learning that can change architecture, representations, procedures, staffing, automation policy or training, with closure evidence. | [S009], [S070], [S071], [S072], [S073], [S076] |
| ECSE-33 | Graceful adaptation, boundary awareness and recoverable degradation | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | High-consequence adaptive systems facing variable demand, uncertainty or disturbances that can exceed nominal plans. | For bounded low-consequence systems, ordinary error handling and restart may provide sufficient resilience. | Engineer visible margins and recoverable modes with explicit trade-offs, rather than claiming generic resilience or relying on heroic adaptation. | [S072], [S073], [S078], [S080], [S086] |
| ECSE-34 | Risk- and complexity-proportional cognitive coordination cheap path | STRONGLY_RETAINED | All candidate CSE controls, especially repetitive low-risk work and small deterministic tools. | Use direct state/effect feedback, a clear owner, simple undo and a concise exception path for low-consequence transparent work. | Preserve the underlying property with the least cognitive and organisational machinery that closes the plausible failure mode. | [S015], [S020], [S024], [S044], [S057], [S069] |
| ECSE-35 | Live decision consumer and lifecycle governance for cognitive artefacts | STRONGLY_RETAINED | Persistent cognitive or coordination artefacts used after initial analysis or deployment. | Do not create a durable artefact for a one-time low-risk decision; record the decision and evidence only. | Treat cognitive artefacts as maintained operational components with configuration, performance and retirement governance. | [S012], [S020], [S024], [S061], [S062], [S071] |
| ECSE-36 | Temporal coordination and explicit pending obligations | JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROPERTY | Asynchronous, cross-session or multi-party work with delayed effects and dependent actions. | For synchronous directly observed work, natural turn-taking and immediate feedback may be sufficient. | Use explicit temporal contracts only at consequential dependency boundaries, with clock/identity semantics and recovery for lateness. | [S025], [S026], [S037], [S052], [S063], [S064] |
| ECSE-37 | Degraded-mode, fallback and source-independence engineering | STATE_MODE_LEGIBILITY_PROPERTY | Consequential systems with sensor/model dependencies, partial failure, failover or manual backup claims. | For low-consequence components, fail closed or restart with clear data-loss semantics instead of elaborate degraded operation. | Use explicit degraded-state contracts and independently credible fallback paths; test transitions and prolonged operation in degradation. | [S008], [S011], [S012], [S073], [S076], [S078] |
| ECSE-38 | Independent cross-check and verification at consequential boundaries | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | Irreversible, high-consequence or error-prone decisions where an independent discriminating check is feasible. | Skip duplicate approval for low-consequence reversible actions or when the second check cannot add independent evidence; use automatic invariants instead. | Use boundary-specific verification whose independence and decision effect are explicit, rather than generic dual sign-off. | [S037], [S042], [S045], [S065], [S067], [S068] |
| ECSE-39 | Work-as-done and local-rationality reconstruction | STRONGLY_RETAINED | Incident analysis, design validation and process change where actual work may differ materially from procedures or models. | For transparent deterministic faults, direct technical diagnosis may suffice; do not force a sociotechnical narrative. | Use field evidence and time-indexed reconstruction to find designable conditions while retaining evidence-based individual accountability where warranted. | [S007], [S070], [S071], [S072], [S073], [S076] |
| ECSE-40 | Organisational, resource and production-pressure context in cognitive design | JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROPERTY | Persistent cognitive/coordination failures, chronic workarounds, staffing stress or conflicts between production and protection. | For isolated, clearly technical interaction defects, fix the defect directly while checking for recurrence context. | Include organisational conditions in the joint work model without making causality so diffuse that no accountable action remains. | [S006], [S070], [S071], [S072], [S073], [S076] |
| ECSE-41 | Decision-centred evaluation of joint-system performance | STRONGLY_RETAINED | Any claim that a new interface, automation policy, explanation or teaming arrangement improves consequential work. | For low-risk design iteration, task completion/error observation may be enough; reserve full comparative trials for material claims. | Make joint decision/action performance the primary endpoint and use cognitive constructs as explanatory measures with stated validity limits. | [S017], [S035], [S036], [S044], [S045], [S046] |
| ECSE-42 | Triangulated measurement of workload, awareness, reliance and coordination | RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM | When a cognitive construct is used to explain, compare or govern a consequential design choice. | Use direct task outcome and observational evidence alone when the construct adds no decision value. | Treat instruments as fallible indicators with construct, measurement and domain validity separated; triangulate only where it changes the engineering decision. | [S029], [S030], [S032], [S033], [S034], [S035] |
| ECSE-43 | Individual situation awareness and SAGAT-style measurement | CONTESTED | Dynamic tasks where knowledge of selected state variables and future evolution is a plausible mediator of performance and probe intrusion is acceptable. | Do not require an SA score when direct state-access, prediction and task-performance measures answer the engineering question more cleanly. | A bounded explanatory construct with explicit ontology, measurement limits and outcome linkage—not a universal system property or post-event label. | [S029], [S030], [S031], [S032], [S033], [S034] |
| ECSE-44 | Distributed or team situation awareness as a named construct | CONTESTED | Multi-person or human-automation work where no one actor should hold all information and coordination depends on distributed access. | Use direct communication, state-access and coordination measures when a global team-SA score adds no causal or decision value. | A bounded account of necessary distributed state and coordination—not an assumption that the system as a whole 'knows' merely because information exists somewhere. | [S025], [S026], [S034], [S037], [S090] |
| ECSE-45 | Full multi-stage Cognitive Work Analysis programme | USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_BUREAUCRATISED | Novel, complex, adaptive work systems where constraints and role possibilities are not already understood and design stakes justify the cost. | Use targeted work-domain/state/coordination modelling for stable or bounded problems; do not require full CWA as a badge. | A modular analysis toolkit whose retained property is valid constraint and work-demand modelling, not completion of every canonical phase. | [S006], [S019], [S020], [S024], [S080] |
| ECSE-46 | Ecological interface design as a canonical display family | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | Continuous dynamic systems with stable physical/functional constraints and expert operators who need off-nominal problem solving. | Use simpler status, trend, state-machine or decision representations for discrete workflows or well-scripted tasks. | One implementation family for the retained constraint-representation property, selected and validated contextually. | [S018], [S021], [S022], [S023] |
| ECSE-47 | Crew Resource Management as a transferable method | DOMAIN_SPECIFIC | Interdependent teams operating under time pressure with asymmetric information and established operational roles. | Do not import aviation scripts wholesale into solitary or loosely coupled work; use targeted coordination practices. | Domain-adapted team training tied to real work, recurrent practice, organisational support and behaviour/outcome evaluation. | [S066], [S067], [S084] |
| ECSE-48 | Standardised handoff or checklist bundle | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | Repeated, consequential handoffs or coordinated procedures with known omission/communication error patterns. | Use a brief direct confirmation for low-risk same-context transfer; do not require a long standard bundle. | A locally validated implementation of explicit state/authority transfer or critical-step verification. | [S065], [S068], [S069] |
| ECSE-49 | Adaptive automation and mixed initiative as a general solution | CONTEXT_DEPENDENT | Variable tasks where relative capability changes are detectable and transition windows are adequate. | Prefer stable allocation when it performs adequately or when adaptation cannot be predicted, explained and recovered. | A selectively deployed policy governed by joint coordination and legible authority transitions, not an evolved-CSE requirement. | [S049], [S050], [S051], [S052], [S053] |
| ECSE-50 | Workload-inferred adaptive authority transfer | UNRESOLVED | Potentially only in validated high-demand settings with stable sensors, strong individual calibration and enough transition time. | Use operator request, task-state triggers, fixed roles, workload shedding or advisory prompts when inference is uncertain. | Not admitted as a general property; at most a context-specific input to a validated multi-signal coordination policy. | [S049], [S050], [S051], [S056], [S057], [S058] |
| ECSE-51 | NASA-TLX or another scalar workload score as the engineering property | USEFUL_BUT_EASILY_GAMED | Comparative studies where subjective workload experience is relevant and respondents can report meaningfully. | Skip it when direct peak-load/performance evidence is decisive or survey burden adds no value. | A measurement instrument with bounded inference, not a requirement or proof that workload is acceptable. | [S056], [S057], [S058] |
| ECSE-52 | Levels-of-automation taxonomy as a design prescription | SUPERSEDED_BY_STRONGER_FORM | Early conceptual comparison of automation alternatives or communication among designers. | For simple designs, directly state who senses, decides, acts, verifies and recovers instead of assigning a level number. | Descriptive scaffolding subordinate to coordination-centred joint-work design. | [S003], [S014], [S017], [S050] |
| ECSE-53 | Static Fitts-list or MABA-MABA allocation as a universal rule | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | No general trigger; a bounded comparative capability table may aid early design for a specific task and technology. | Directly model task demands, interdependencies, state, authority, residual work and recovery. | Rejected as a universal rule; superseded by context-sensitive coordination and joint-system evaluation. | [S002], [S015], [S016] |
| ECSE-54 | Ceremonial human-in-the-loop click or nominal override | CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY | None as a stand-alone control; approval may be useful only when property 12's capability conditions hold. | Remove the click/override and expose direct undo or safe automatic bounds for low-risk work. | No general property; replaced by genuine intervention capability, authority alignment and takeover feasibility. | [S008], [S010], [S012], [S038], [S045], [S048] |
| ECSE-55 | Maximise trust in automation | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | No general trigger. | For deterministic guaranteed functions, present guarantees and failure semantics rather than trust appeals. | Replaced by property 16 and property 29. | [S013], [S039], [S040], [S041], [S042], [S043] |
| ECSE-56 | More information, transparency or explanation is universally better | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | No general trigger; additional information is justified only by a live decision or coordination failure. | Use direct state/effect, a concise limit or an exception cue when that closes the failure mode. | Replaced by properties 7-10 and 28, with attention/load constraints. | [S044], [S045], [S046], [S047], [S048], [S086] |
| ECSE-57 | Visible mode annunciator or dashboard as sufficient mode understanding | CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY | A mode label is useful when modes change action semantics, but never sufficient by itself. | For single-mode or directly perceptible systems, show action/effect without a separate dashboard. | No stand-alone property; subsumed by properties 7 and 8. | [S009], [S012], [S076], [S079], [S087] |
| ECSE-58 | Human error as a terminal causal explanation | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | No terminal-cause trigger; individual action may remain one causal factor after deeper analysis. | For a simple deliberate unauthorised act with clear evidence, document agency directly but still assess control conditions proportionally. | Rejected as terminal cause; replaced by time-indexed local-rationality and joint-system analysis. | [S070], [S071], [S072], [S076], [S080] |
| ECSE-59 | Display of chain-of-thought or internal reasoning as required transparency | CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY | No general trigger; use explanatory information only when it supports verification or coordination. | For deterministic actions, expose rule and evidence; for opaque models, provide validated behavioural/limit evidence rather than narrative internals. | No general property; replaced by decision-linked legibility and verifiability. | [S044], [S045], [S046], [S047] |
| ECSE-60 | More alerts or maximum sensitivity as more awareness | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | No general trigger; sensitivity must follow consequence, base rate, response and attention cost. | Use passive status/logging for low-urgency conditions and invariant automatic protection when human response is infeasible. | Rejected; replaced by actionable alerting and lifecycle management. | [S059], [S060], [S061], [S062], [S087] |
| ECSE-61 | Acknowledgement, checklist completion or message receipt as understanding | CEREMONY_NOT_GENERAL_PROPERTY | No stand-alone trigger; acknowledgement is useful as one transition in a broader coordination contract. | For low-risk notices, receipt may be sufficient; do not pretend it proves more. | No general property; subsumed by grounding, handoff, feedback closure and verification. | [S037], [S065], [S068], [S069] |
| ECSE-62 | Minimise workload as a universal design objective | REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED | No universal trigger. | For simple routine work, reduce unnecessary steps; for monitoring/recovery roles, ensure meaningful engagement or remove the role. | Rejected; replaced by peak/reserve, underload and residual-work properties. | [S008], [S010], [S017], [S050], [S056], [S057] |

## Complete property cards

### ECSE-01 — Joint cognitive work system as the unit of design

- **PROPERTY_ID:** ECSE-01
- **PROPERTY_NAME:** Joint cognitive work system as the unit of design
- **HISTORICAL_ORIGIN:** Hollnagel and Woods (1983), Rasmussen et al. (1994), Hutchins (1995), Hollnagel and Woods (2005)
- **LINEAGE_CLASS:** COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE; DISTRIBUTED_COGNITION_LINEAGE
- **ORIGINAL_FORM:** Analyse cognition and control across the coupled human-machine-work system rather than treating the person as an isolated component.
- **PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED:** Local component optimisation can degrade system-level coordination, conceal displaced work, and leave no owner for coupling failures.
- **COGNITIVE_OR_COORDINATION_FAILURE_MODE:** Component passes mask interaction failures, hidden coordination work, conflicting local goals and unowned transitions.
- **FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT:** Component passes mask interaction failures, hidden coordination work, conflicting local goals and unowned transitions.
- **MECHANISM:** Model people, automation, procedures, representations and organisational supports as interdependent contributors to one work function; evaluate joint outcomes and coordination costs.
- **TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT:** Consequential work in which decisions, representations, authority or control are distributed across two or more participants or artefacts.
- **NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH:** For a low-consequence, single-actor, transparent deterministic operation, document the actor, state and effect without constructing a full joint-system model.
- **DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS:** A stable-enough work boundary, access to work-as-done, and a named engineering consumer.
- **STATE_OR_MODE_PRECONDITIONS:** Current shared and private state relevant to coordination must be identifiable.
- **AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS:** Authority and accountability must remain assignable even when cognition is distributed.
- **TIMING_OR_ATTENTION_PRECONDITIONS:** Temporal coupling and decision deadlines must be represented.
- **EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF:** Fewer interaction surprises and a defensible explanation of how the whole work function succeeds or fails.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** System architect, operations owner, safety/assurance owner, and the actors who perform the work.
- **KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES:** The boundary can become so expansive that analysis loses actionability or responsibility becomes diffuse.; Over-application can add cognitive load, delay, false authority or bureaucracy when the trigger does not hold.
- **IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS:** The boundary can become so expansive that analysis loses actionability or responsibility becomes diffuse.
- **HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED:** From component human factors to cognitive engineering, distributed cognition and joint cognitive systems.
- **MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM:** Define the work system boundary, cognitive functions, authority, information flows, dependencies, timing and adaptation; test joint performance, not merely component usability.
- **CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY:** A system map, dashboard or workshop is not the property; the property is engineering the consequential couplings and evaluating joint outcomes.
- **CURRENT_STATUS:** JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROPERTY
- **EVIDENCE_STRENGTH:** OVERALL=STRONG_WITH_CONTEXTUAL_IMPLEMENTATION_LIMITS; HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH=HIGH; CONSTRUCT_VALIDITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; MEASUREMENT_VALIDITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE; LAB_EXPERIMENT_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; FIELD_EMPIRICAL_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; ACCIDENT_OR_INCIDENT_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; DOMAIN_PRACTICE_STRENGTH=HIGH_IN_ESTABLISHED_DOMAINS; TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH_AT_MECHANISM_LEVEL; ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY=MODERATE; payoff depends on consequence, coupling, timing and implementation quality; CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH=MODERATE; mainly limits universal implementations rather than the underlying property; RATIONALE=Primary evidence: Cross-domain mechanism evidence and case evidence are strong; controlled comparative evidence for any single modelling notation is weaker. Contrary/limiting evidence: Human-AI combinations do not show synergy on average, so joint-system framing is a design obligation, not evidence that pairing is beneficial.
- **PRIMARY_SOURCES:** [S005], [S006], [S007], [S025], [S026], [S027], [S028], [S038], [S052], [S080], [S086], [S090]
- **CRITICAL_SOURCES:** [S015], [S048]
- **EMPIRICAL_OR_DOMAIN_EVIDENCE:** Cross-domain mechanism evidence and case evidence are strong; controlled comparative evidence for any single modelling notation is weaker.
- **CONTRARY_EVIDENCE:** Human-AI combinations do not show synergy on average, so joint-system framing is a design obligation, not evidence that pairing is beneficial.
- **OPEN_QUESTIONS:** How should boundaries be kept actionable in highly networked organisations and multi-agent ecosystems?
- **JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROFILE:** APPLICABILITY=PRIMARY_OR_MATERIAL; PROPERTY=Joint cognitive work system as the unit of design; WORK_SYSTEM=The bounded set of people, automation/agents, procedures, representations, organisational supports and environment that jointly performs the consequential work.; HUMAN_ROLE=Sense, interpret, decide, coordinate, challenge, adapt, verify or recover only to the extent supported by competence, state access, authority and time.; AUTOMATION_OR_AGENT_ROLE=Sense, transform, recommend, act, monitor or coordinate within explicit limits, state semantics and recovery obligations.; SHARED_OR_DISTRIBUTED_STATE=Current shared and private state relevant to coordination must be identifiable.; COORDINATION_REQUIREMENT=Model people, automation, procedures, representations and organisational supports as interdependent contributors to one work function; evaluate joint outcomes and coordination costs.; AUTHORITY_RELATION=Authority and accountability must remain assignable even when cognition is distributed.; TEMPORAL_REQUIREMENT=Temporal coupling and decision deadlines must be represented.; FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED=The boundary can become so expansive that analysis loses actionability or responsibility becomes diffuse.; CHEAP_PATH=For a low-consequence, single-actor, transparent deterministic operation, document the actor, state and effect without constructing a full joint-system model.; MATURE_FORM=Define the work system boundary, cognitive functions, authority, information flows, dependencies, timing and adaptation; test joint performance, not merely component usability.
- **STATE_MODE_LEGIBILITY_PROFILE:** APPLICABILITY=PRIMARY_OR_MATERIAL; PROPERTY=Joint cognitive work system as the unit of design; DECISION_RELEVANT_STATE=Current shared and private state relevant to coordination must be identifiable.; WHO_NEEDS_IT=System architect, operations owner, safety/assurance owner, and the actors who perform the work.; WHEN_IT_IS_NEEDED=Temporal coupling and decision deadlines must be represented.; REPRESENTATION=Use the smallest task-congruent representation that makes consequences and action possibilities legible; provide drill-down rather than indiscriminate detail.; FRESHNESS_REQUIREMENT=Age/as-of time and update semantics are explicit whenever staleness could change action.; PROVENANCE_REQUIREMENT=Distinguish measured, inferred, reported and model-generated claims; preserve source/transform lineage when it changes verification.; TRANSITION_VISIBILITY=Pending, armed, committed, executing, completed, failed, degraded and reverted states are distinguished when applicable.; UNCERTAINTY_VISIBILITY=Uncertainty, missingness, degradation and scope limits are shown only to the degree needed for correct reliance or action.; FAILURE_MODE=Component passes mask interaction failures, hidden coordination work, conflicting local goals and unowned transitions.; CHEAP_PATH=For a low-consequence, single-actor, transparent deterministic operation, document the actor, state and effect without constructing a full joint-system model.; MATURE_FORM=Define the work system boundary, cognitive functions, authority, information flows, dependencies, timing and adaptation; test joint performance, not merely component usability.
- **ATTENTION_ESCALATION_PROFILE:** APPLICABILITY=SECONDARY_OR_NOT_PRIMARY; PROPERTY=Joint cognitive work system as the unit of design; ATTENTION_TARGET=The condition, obligation, transition or discrepancy that can still change action.; WHO_MUST_NOTICE=System architect, operations owner, safety/assurance owner, and the actors who perform the work.; TRIGGER=Consequential work in which decisions, representations, authority or control are distributed across two or more participants or artefacts.; PRIORITY_BASIS=Time-to-consequence, reversibility, uncertainty, competing demand and available response—not salience alone.; ROUTING=Route to the responsible and capable actor; avoid broadcast when no broad action is required.; TIMING=Temporal coupling and decision deadlines must be represented.; ESCALATION=Escalate on non-response, worsening condition, loss of capability or unresolved discrepancy with explicit ownership.; ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_SEMANTICS=Receipt, comprehension evidence, acceptance, action and resolution remain distinct states.; LOAD_AND_INTERRUPTION_EFFECT=Not a primary attention-control property; avoid adding unnecessary interruption.; FAILURE_MODE=Component passes mask interaction failures, hidden coordination work, conflicting local goals and unowned transitions.; CHEAP_PATH=For a low-consequence, single-actor, transparent deterministic operation, document the actor, state and effect without constructing a full joint-system model.; MATURE_FORM=Define the work system boundary, cognitive functions, authority, information flows, dependencies, timing and adaptation; test joint performance, not merely component usability.

### ECSE-02 — Decision-relevant work-domain and constraint modelling

- **PROPERTY_ID:** ECSE-02
- **PROPERTY_NAME:** Decision-relevant work-domain and constraint modelling
- **HISTORICAL_ORIGIN:** Rasmussen's abstraction hierarchy; Rasmussen, Pejtersen and Goodstein (1994); Naikar's CWA development
- **LINEAGE_CLASS:** COGNITIVE_WORK_ANALYSIS_LINEAGE; ECOLOGICAL_INTERFACE_LINEAGE
- **ORIGINAL_FORM:** Represent purposes, values, functions, processes, physical resources and means-ends links independently of one prescribed task sequence.
- **PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED:** Procedure-only descriptions hide invariant constraints and give operators little support when conditions depart from the nominal script.
- **COGNITIVE_OR_COORDINATION_FAILURE_MODE:** Hidden constraints, brittle procedural compliance, diagnosis by memorised symptom, and unrecognised boundary approach.
- **FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT:** Hidden constraints, brittle procedural compliance, diagnosis by memorised symptom, and unrecognised boundary approach.
- **MECHANISM:** Elicit the constraints, boundaries, resources, trade-offs and means-ends relations that determine which actions remain viable; expose the minimum subset needed by live decisions.
- **TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT:** Complex, variable or safety/consequence-sensitive work in which unanticipated states or multiple strategies are plausible.
- **NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH:** For stable routine work, a concise state-transition model, invariant list or decision table may preserve the property without a full CWA programme.
- **DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS:** Domain expertise, access to actual work, a model owner and change-control linkage.
- **STATE_OR_MODE_PRECONDITIONS:** The operational state variables and constraints represented must be measurable or inferable with known uncertainty.
- **AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS:** The model must distinguish who may trade off which goals and who can cross or relax constraints.
- **TIMING_OR_ATTENTION_PRECONDITIONS:** Constraints needed under disturbance must be available before action deadlines.
- **EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF:** Better diagnosis and adaptation in novel states; fewer invalid actions caused by missing system relationships.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Interface designer, procedure designer, training owner, controller/operator and architecture reviewer.
- **KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES:** Full CWA can be costly, analyst-dependent, hard to validate and liable to staleness as software and organisation change.; Over-application can add cognitive load, delay, false authority or bureaucracy when the trigger does not hold.
- **IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS:** Full CWA can be costly, analyst-dependent, hard to validate and liable to staleness as software and organisation change.
- **HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED:** From comprehensive work-domain analysis toward proportional constraint modelling and live maintenance.
- **MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM:** Maintain an auditable, decision-consumed constraint model at the smallest useful granularity; link representations and procedures to it.
- **CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY:** The multi-stage CWA artefact is optional; the maintained decision-relevant constraint representation is the property.
- **CURRENT_STATUS:** RETAINED_IN_EVOLVED_FORM
- **EVIDENCE_STRENGTH:** OVERALL=MODERATE_TO_STRONG; HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH=HIGH; CONSTRUCT_VALIDITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; MEASUREMENT_VALIDITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE_OR_NOT_CENTRAL; LAB_EXPERIMENT_STRENGTH=MODERATE; FIELD_EMPIRICAL_STRENGTH=MODERATE; ACCIDENT_OR_INCIDENT_STRENGTH=LOW_TO_MODERATE_OR_INDIRECT; DOMAIN_PRACTICE_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH_IN_SOME_DOMAINS; TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE_AT_MECHANISM_LEVEL; ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH=MODERATE; RATIONALE=Primary evidence: EID/CWA studies support design value in complex control domains but comparative field evidence and cost-effectiveness remain uneven. Contrary/limiting evidence: Simpler task analysis or state models may equal the payoff in stable domains; poor analyst choices can encode work-as-imagined.
- **PRIMARY_SOURCES:** [S004], [S006], [S018], [S019], [S020], [S021], [S022], [S023], [S024], [S080]
- **CRITICAL_SOURCES:** [S024], [S023]
- **EMPIRICAL_OR_DOMAIN_EVIDENCE:** EID/CWA studies support design value in complex control domains but comparative field evidence and cost-effectiveness remain uneven.
- **CONTRARY_EVIDENCE:** Simpler task analysis or state models may equal the payoff in stable domains; poor analyst choices can encode work-as-imagined.
- **OPEN_QUESTIONS:** What validation and maintenance regimes best detect when a work-domain model has ceased to match work?
- **JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROFILE:** APPLICABILITY=PRIMARY_OR_MATERIAL; PROPERTY=Decision-relevant work-domain and constraint modelling; WORK_SYSTEM=The bounded set of people, automation/agents, procedures, representations, organisational supports and environment that jointly performs the consequential work.; HUMAN_ROLE=Sense, interpret, decide, coordinate, challenge, adapt, verify or recover only to the extent supported by competence, state access, authority and time.; AUTOMATION_OR_AGENT_ROLE=Sense, transform, recommend, act, monitor or coordinate within explicit limits, state semantics and recovery obligations.; SHARED_OR_DISTRIBUTED_STATE=The operational state variables and constraints represented must be measurable or inferable with known uncertainty.; COORDINATION_REQUIREMENT=Elicit the constraints, boundaries, resources, trade-offs and means-ends relations that determine which actions remain viable; expose the minimum subset needed by live decisions.; AUTHORITY_RELATION=The model must distinguish who may trade off which goals and who can cross or relax constraints.; TEMPORAL_REQUIREMENT=Constraints needed under disturbance must be available before action deadlines.; FAILURE_IF_OVER_APPLIED=Full CWA can be costly, analyst-dependent, hard to validate and liable to staleness as software and organisation change.; CHEAP_PATH=For stable routine work, a concise state-transition model, invariant list or decision table may preserve the property without a full CWA programme.; MATURE_FORM=Maintain an auditable, decision-consumed constraint model at the smallest useful granularity; link representations and procedures to it.
- **STATE_MODE_LEGIBILITY_PROFILE:** APPLICABILITY=PRIMARY_OR_MATERIAL; PROPERTY=Decision-relevant work-domain and constraint modelling; DECISION_RELEVANT_STATE=The operational state variables and constraints represented must be measurable or inferable with known uncertainty.; WHO_NEEDS_IT=Interface designer, procedure designer, training owner, controller/operator and architecture reviewer.; WHEN_IT_IS_NEEDED=Constraints needed under disturbance must be available before action deadlines.; REPRESENTATION=Use the smallest task-congruent representation that makes consequences and action possibilities legible; provide drill-down rather than indiscriminate detail.; FRESHNESS_REQUIREMENT=Age/as-of time and update semantics are explicit whenever staleness could change action.; PROVENANCE_REQUIREMENT=Distinguish measured, inferred, reported and model-generated claims; preserve source/transform lineage when it changes verification.; TRANSITION_VISIBILITY=Pending, armed, committed, executing, completed, failed, degraded and reverted states are distinguished when applicable.; UNCERTAINTY_VISIBILITY=Uncertainty, missingness, degradation and scope limits are shown only to the degree needed for correct reliance or action.; FAILURE_MODE=Hidden constraints, brittle procedural compliance, diagnosis by memorised symptom, and unrecognised boundary approach.; CHEAP_PATH=For stable routine work, a concise state-transition model, invariant list or decision table may preserve the property without a full CWA programme.; MATURE_FORM=Maintain an auditable, decision-consumed constraint model at the smallest useful granularity; link representations and procedures to it.

### ECSE-03 — Distributed representations and external cognitive support

- **PROPERTY_ID:** ECSE-03
- **PROPERTY_NAME:** Distributed representations and external cognitive support
- **HISTORICAL_ORIGIN:** Hutchins' studies of navigation and cockpit speed representations; cognitive engineering research on tools
- **LINEAGE_CLASS:** DISTRIBUTED_COGNITION_LINEAGE; COGNITIVE_SYSTEMS_ENGINEERING_LINEAGE
- **ORIGINAL_FORM:** Treat representations, marks, displays, procedures and shared artefacts as functional parts of remembering, calculating and coordinating.
- **PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED:** Design that assumes all relevant state is held in individual memory creates omission, reconstruction and coordination failures.
- **COGNITIVE_OR_COORDINATION_FAILURE_MODE:** Prospective-memory loss, duplicated work, inconsistent local copies and handoff amnesia.
- **FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT:** Prospective-memory loss, duplicated work, inconsistent local copies and handoff amnesia.
- **MECHANISM:** Place stable, inspectable and updateable state in shared artefacts; make transformations and dependencies visible and preserve provenance across handoffs.
- **TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT:** Work with multi-step obligations, interruptions, team coordination, long time spans or high memory demand.
- **NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH:** Do not externalise trivial facts when the representation costs more attention than it saves; use a small status marker or no artefact.
- **DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS:** Clear update authority, identity, version/freshness semantics and retirement rules.
- **STATE_OR_MODE_PRECONDITIONS:** State stored externally must be distinguishable from inferred or unverified claims.
- **AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS:** Write/update/approve permissions must match responsibility.
- **TIMING_OR_ATTENTION_PRECONDITIONS:** The representation must be accessible at the point of decision and resumable after interruption.
- **EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF:** Reduced memory burden and more reliable continuity across people, sessions and disturbances.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** Operators, coordinators, shift leads and downstream decision makers.
- **KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES:** External representations can be stale, inconsistent, overly authoritative, insecure or cognitively expensive.; Over-application can add cognitive load, delay, false authority or bureaucracy when the trigger does not hold.
- **IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS:** External representations can be stale, inconsistent, overly authoritative, insecure or cognitively expensive.
- **HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED:** From display/readability concerns to cognition distributed across people and artefacts.
- **MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM:** Design external memory around live tasks, ownership, update semantics, freshness and recovery; test whether it reduces errors rather than merely adding documentation.
- **CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY:** A shared document is not sufficient; the property includes semantics, ownership, freshness and actual decision use.
- **CURRENT_STATUS:** STRONGLY_RETAINED
- **EVIDENCE_STRENGTH:** OVERALL=STRONG_WITH_CONTEXTUAL_IMPLEMENTATION_LIMITS; HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH=HIGH; CONSTRUCT_VALIDITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; MEASUREMENT_VALIDITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE; LAB_EXPERIMENT_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; FIELD_EMPIRICAL_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; ACCIDENT_OR_INCIDENT_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; DOMAIN_PRACTICE_STRENGTH=HIGH_IN_ESTABLISHED_DOMAINS; TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH_AT_MECHANISM_LEVEL; ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY=MODERATE; payoff depends on consequence, coupling, timing and implementation quality; CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH=MODERATE; mainly limits universal implementations rather than the underlying property; RATIONALE=Primary evidence: Strong observational and experimental mechanism support; effect sizes depend on representation quality and task coupling. Contrary/limiting evidence: Shared artefacts may create false consensus or become a single stale source of error.
- **PRIMARY_SOURCES:** [S007], [S025], [S026], [S027], [S037], [S063], [S064], [S065], [S086]
- **CRITICAL_SOURCES:** [S086]
- **EMPIRICAL_OR_DOMAIN_EVIDENCE:** Strong observational and experimental mechanism support; effect sizes depend on representation quality and task coupling.
- **CONTRARY_EVIDENCE:** Shared artefacts may create false consensus or become a single stale source of error.
- **OPEN_QUESTIONS:** How can shared state remain authoritative without suppressing legitimate local dissent or privacy needs?

### ECSE-04 — Coordination design beyond function allocation

- **PROPERTY_ID:** ECSE-04
- **PROPERTY_NAME:** Coordination design beyond function allocation
- **HISTORICAL_ORIGIN:** Criticism of Fitts-list allocation; MABA-MABA critique; joint-activity and coactive-design work
- **LINEAGE_CLASS:** HUMAN_AUTOMATION_LINEAGE; CONVERGENT_ENGINEERING
- **ORIGINAL_FORM:** Replace one-time assignment of functions with design of dependencies, communication, observability, predictability and recovery between performers.
- **PROBLEM_IT_ADDRESSED:** A function can be allocated correctly in isolation yet fail because prerequisites, transitions, exceptions and residual work are uncoordinated.
- **COGNITIVE_OR_COORDINATION_FAILURE_MODE:** Leftover tasks, responsibility gaps, duplicated control, conflicting action and brittle handoffs.
- **FAILURE_MODE_IT_TRIES_TO_PREVENT:** Leftover tasks, responsibility gaps, duplicated control, conflicting action and brittle handoffs.
- **MECHANISM:** For each interdependent function, engineer who initiates, informs, confirms, monitors, challenges, completes and recovers it, including transition load.
- **TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT:** Any consequential split of work between humans, automation, teams or agents.
- **NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH:** A fully encapsulated, deterministic service with verified input/output contracts may need only interface and failure semantics rather than rich teaming protocol.
- **DEPENDENCIES_OR_PRECONDITIONS:** A task dependency model and explicit authority/feedback semantics.
- **STATE_OR_MODE_PRECONDITIONS:** Each participant needs state sufficient to coordinate its contribution.
- **AUTHORITY_PRECONDITIONS:** Initiative, veto, escalation and final-decision rights must be explicit in operation.
- **TIMING_OR_ATTENTION_PRECONDITIONS:** Coordination must fit the pace and consequences of the work.
- **EXPECTED_ENGINEERING_PAYOFF:** Lower coordination debt and fewer failures at the seams between nominally capable components.
- **DECISION_OR_CONSUMER:** System designer, automation-policy owner and operational team.
- **KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES:** Over-coordination can create latency, excessive confirmation and role ambiguity; dynamic roles can become unpredictable.; Over-application can add cognitive load, delay, false authority or bureaucracy when the trigger does not hold.
- **IMPORTANT_CRITICISMS:** Over-coordination can create latency, excessive confirmation and role ambiguity; dynamic roles can become unpredictable.
- **HOW_THE_PROPERTY_EVOLVED:** Static allocation was preserved as descriptive scaffolding but superseded as the complete design problem.
- **MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM:** Use function allocation as an input, then close the coordination contracts, transitions, feedback and recovery for the joint activity.
- **CEREMONY_VS_PROPERTY:** A RACI chart or automation-level label is not enough; the property is an executable, timed coordination relationship.
- **CURRENT_STATUS:** JOINT_COGNITIVE_SYSTEM_PROPERTY
- **EVIDENCE_STRENGTH:** OVERALL=STRONG_WITH_CONTEXTUAL_IMPLEMENTATION_LIMITS; HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE_STRENGTH=HIGH; CONSTRUCT_VALIDITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; MEASUREMENT_VALIDITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE; LAB_EXPERIMENT_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; FIELD_EMPIRICAL_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; ACCIDENT_OR_INCIDENT_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH; DOMAIN_PRACTICE_STRENGTH=HIGH_IN_ESTABLISHED_DOMAINS; TRANSFERABILITY_STRENGTH=MODERATE_TO_HIGH_AT_MECHANISM_LEVEL; ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY=MODERATE; payoff depends on consequence, coupling, timing and implementation quality; CONTRARY_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH=MODERATE; mainly limits universal implementations rather than the underlying property; RATIONALE=Primary evidence: Historical, theoretical and field evidence strongly supports the failure mechanism; universal superiority of any one coordination framework is unproven. Contrary/limiting evidence: In tightly coupled high-speed control, excessive negotiation can be worse than stable pre-authorised roles.
- **PRIMARY_SOURCES:** [S002], [S003], [S014], [S015], [S016], [S038], [S052], [S053], [S088]
- **CRITICAL_SOURCES:** [S008], [S015], [S048]
- **EMPIRICAL_OR_DOMAIN_EVIDENCE:** Historical, theoretical and field evidence strongly supports the failure mechanism; universal superiority of any one coordination framework is unproven.
- **CONTRARY_EVIDENCE:** In tightly coupled high-speed control, excessive negotiation can be worse than stable pre-authorised roles.
- **OPEN_QUESTIONS:** Which coordination contracts can be verified formally without excluding adaptive work?
